newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH IMPORT DEPOSIT PLAN MISSES MARK - ANALYST.
newsitem.headline: CZECH IMPORT DEPOSIT PLAN MISSES MARK - ANALYST.

text.p: The Czech government's recently announced import deposit plan should have an immediate effect on goods coming into the country, but fails to address structural problems in industry, a leading economist said on Wednesday.

Jiri Krovak, head of economic research at Wood and Company, told Reuters the plan, which forces importers to place 20 percent of the value of imported consumer goods into non- interest bearing accounts for six months, may hurt more than help the economy.

"It should have an immediate effect because it's really a short-term administrative move," he said in an interview at the FIBEX international banking and finance exhibition in the Czech second city of Brno.

"(But) there is no reason to administratively restrict imports and in the long-term it is not good for the economy because it artificially protects domestic producers. It doesn't force them to increase their competitiveness," he added.
The import deposit plan, announced last week as part of a government plan to kick start the economy and reverse the trend of a widening trade deficit, took effect on Monday.
But Krovak said the plan does not address the core problem of the economy which "is that even with booming domestic demand, domestic producers are not capable of meeting the demand".

"They (producers) simply are not flexible, they do not adjust output with the structure of demand. This is why the trade deficit is of a structural nature. This is turn is caused by a low degree of restructuring, due to the ownership structure of firms that has developed here," he said.

Krovak added that the measures will affect mostly small and medium-sized importers who must find ways to settle the administrative side of the plan, adding that it should affect nearly half of monthly imports.
"This is totally in contradiction with the government's declared support for small and medium sized businesses," he said.
